cultural.vision_reason: This is a classic strip-woven kente cloth in purple with yellow/multicolor geometric weft patterns, matching the Asante (Ashanti) textile tradition described in the metadata.

physical.title: cloth; textile
physical.summary: Man's cloth (Asante kente) formed of 21 narrow strips of  hand-woven imported rayon and cotton, hand-sewn together selvedge to selvedge. The warp is the same in all the strips: a base of purple cotton with yellow stripes running through it; three yellow stripes have also been introduced into the weft. Both ends of the cloth have complex weft-faced matching patterns, and the warp ends have been left loose to form a fringe. Across the face of the central area of the cloth have been introduced regularly-spaced weft blocks arranged to give a chequerboard alternation with the warp pattern. The weft blocks themselves are made of white, green, red and yellow rayon yarn, with varied discontinuous supplementary weft patterns introduced between flanking solid blocks of colour.
